key_insight: Replacing per-head keys and values with a shared low-rank latent KV cache (Multi-Head Latent Attention, MLA) dramatically reduces the memory and latency of the KV layout for long-rollout autoregressive video diffusion, enabling minute-scale generation while preserving modeling capacity.
problem_solved: Long-rollout causal video diffusion is bottlenecked by a large per-head KV cache that scales poorly in memory and latency for minute-scale streaming; the paper removes this dominant inefficiency in the KV layout.
method: Introduce Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA): a shared low-rank latent K/V representation used across attention heads instead of separate per-head K/V tensors.
Factorize and compress the KV cache into a small set of latent basis vectors and light-weight projection/reconstruction steps, with efficient incremental updates for autoregressive rollouts.
Integrate MLA into sliding-window/streaming diffusion pipeline while preserving positional conditioning and attention routing to keep sample quality.
impact: VideoMLA cuts streaming memory and inference latency for autoregressive video diffusion, making minute-scale generation practically feasible on fewer resources and enabling real-time or long-horizon video synthesis workflows for practitioners.

paper_title: VideoMLA: Low-Rank Latent KV Cache for Minute-Scale Autoregressive Video Diffusion
paper_authors: Hidir Yesiltepe, Jiazhen Hu, Tuna Han Salih Meral, Adil Kaan Akan, Kaan Oktay
